choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation: B is correct. If Doris is 20 years old, as well as twice as old as Emily, then Emily is 10 years old and not 40 years old.

questions.question:
Read the facts and determine if they prove the conclusion or not.

FACTS:
• A box contains many marbles.
• Some of the marbles are green.
• Almost half of the marbles are red.
• All of the marbles that are neither green nor red are orange.

CONCLUSION: There are more green marbles than orange marbles in the box.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is - (C)

Since we do not know the number of green and orange marbles (some are green, all that are neither green nor red are orange), we have no way of knowing if there are more green marbles than orange marbles or more orange marbles than green marbles, or an equal number of green and orange marbles.

questions.question:

CONCLUSION: It did not rain this morning.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation: A is correct. Mark always jogs around his neighborhood unless it is raining or snowing. If Mark jogged around his neighborhood this morning then it must have neither rained nor snowed this morning.

questions.question:

choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation: B is correct. If Jason is late to the meeting then Kevin will not get home from work on time because he will have to work late. Lois will cook dinner for Kevin only if Kevin gets home from work on time Thus, if Lois cooked dinner for Kevin, Jason could not have come late to the meeting.

questions.question:

CONCLUSION: Fred works in the upper half of the office building.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation: A is correct. If Gary works on the eighth floor and Fred works two floors below Gary, then Fred works on the sixth floor. If the office building has ten floors, then Fred works in the upper half of the office building (floors five to ten).

questions.question:

CONCLUSION: the next morning Samantha is tired.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation:
A is correct. Samantha is tired the next morning.
We can come to this conclusion because the last sentence states that Tom did not go to the concert, which means Ursula did go. If Ursula went it means Roger went, and roger took Samantha with him. Thus, Samantha is tired the next morning.

questions.question:
FACTS: Four students (Wendy, Irving, Tessa and Sheldon) all took a test. No two students received the same score. Wendy did not get the highest score. The student who received the lowest score was Tessa. Irving got a 93 and Sheldon got a 77. The average score was 82.

CONCLUSION: Wendy's score was not below the average score.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation: A is correct. If the average score for four students is 82, then their total score is 328. Irving got a 93 and Sheldon got a 77 leaving 158 points to be split between Wendy and Tessa. If Tessa got the lowest score, the highest score Tessa could get is 76 which leaves 82 points for Wendy. Therefore, Wendy's score was not below the average score.

CONCLUSION: Ben is the married man.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation: B is correct. If Al is sitting to the left of the married woman and Denise is sitting between Carol and Ben, then Carol is the married woman. This means that Al is sitting to Carol's left. Carol is sitting to Denise's left. Denise is sitting to Ben's left. Ben is sitting to Al's left. This means that Al and Denise are sitting across from each other and Carol and Ben are sitting across from each other. If the married people are not sitting across from each other, then Carol must be married to Al. Therefore, Ben is not the married man.

questions.question:
FACTS: On Monday, the stock market gained 200 points. On Tuesday, the stock market lost 1% of its value. On Wednesday, the stock market gained 1% of its value. On Thursday, the stock market lost 200 points. On Friday, the stock market gained 1 point.

CONCLUSION: The stock market ended the week higher than it started the week.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation:
C is correct. We can't know if the stock market ended higher or lower without knowing where it started. For example, assume the stock market started at 1000. On Monday, it closed at 1200. On Tuesday, it closed at 1188. On Wednesday, it closed at 1199.88. On Thursday, it closed at 999.88. On Friday, it closed at 1000.88. In this case, the stock market did end the week higher than it started the week.

Now assume the stock market started at 10000. On Monday, it closed at 10200. On Tuesday, it closed at 10098. On Wednesday, it closed at 10198.98. On Thursday, it closed at 9998.98. On Friday, it closed at 9999.98. In this case, the stock market did not end the week higher than it started the week.

questions.explanation: B is correct. Angela, though a female name on Earth, has three syllables. Only males have names with an odd number of syllables on the planet Glorp. Therefore, Angela is a male.

CONCLUSION: Josh's wallet contains exact change for a $20 bill.
choices: The facts neither prove nor disprove the conclusion.
questions.explanation:
C is correct. If Josh's wallet contains only 1 $1 bill, then there are also 2 $5 bills which is not enough to make change for a $20 bill. If Josh's wallet contains 2 $1 bills, then there are 4 $5 bills which is enough to make change for a $20 bill.

Since the amount of bills in his wallet is not specified, we cannot ascertain whether he has exact change for a 20 dollar bill.

Note that the conclusion did not say that Josh's wallet contains exact change for a $20 bill and nothing else. That is, it is possible that Josh has exact change for a $20 bill (for example, four $5 bills) as well as other bills (for example, two $1 bills).

If Bill is not married to the woman who likes to play tennis, and we know that Bill is married to Connie, then Connie doesn't like to play tennis. That leaves Abbie as the one who likes to play tennis.

Note that the mention of "the woman who likes to play tennis" means one of the women necessarily likes to play tennis. For this reason, C cannot be the correct answer.

All airplanes that don't stop in Spain fly to India. Since the first airplane didn't stop in Spain, it must have flown to India.

questions.question: People who play instruments don't sing. All singers play instruments. Which of the following statements must be true?
questions.explanation:
The answer is B, "singers don't sing", as illustrated above.

Note that answer C is incorrect because "some" is a word used in existence statements, yet existence is not evident from the premises. we know that if there are singers, they play instruments, and therefore don't sing (the two premises combined) but we cannot deduce that there are actually singers. Answer C claims that there exist some singers and that they don't sing. However, the two premises in the question are theoretical ones and according to formal logic rules, it is impossible to infer existence from a theoretical premise.

questions.question:
Read the five statements below.

1. Jennifer runs faster than Robin, but slower than Grace.
2. Emma is the slowest.
3. Grace and Harriet run at the same speed.
4. Harriet runs faster than Emma.
5. Robin runs faster than Andrea.

Which of the statements above must be true if it is followed that Harriet runs faster than Andrea?
questions.explanation:
The answer is 1, 3, 5.

When addressing this question it is advisable to first take a look at the answers and see just how many statements we are supposed to need: in this case, only three.
Now we can look at the statements and gather those that are relevant to the conclusion we are presented with. We know that Harriet runs faster than Andrea, therefore it makes sense to figure out the relationships that relate to this information. We can arrange our data in the form of a list.
Statement 1 gives information about Robin and Grace. We can write it down and move on to the next statement.
Statement 2 gives us new information but we don't know yet how helpful it is, thus we should continue and see what we can gather from other statements.
Statement 3 seems relevant since it involves Harriet and Grace, who we encountered in the first statement.
Statement 4 seems redundant since we already know that Emma is the slowest (statement 2), therefore we can safely rule out statement 4 from our answer, which means answers A (2+3+4) and B (1+3+4) are wrong.
Now we need only compare answers C and D:
Answer C states we need statements 1, 2 and 3, but that means we have information missing since we don't know the relationship between all the characters. Therefore, answer D is the correct one and we can easily assert that it is true by looking at statement 5 and the information it gives us in addition to statements 1 and 3: If Harriet and Grace run at the same pace, Jennifer runs faster than Robyn and slower than Grace, and Robin runs faster than Andrea, it clearly follows that Grace runs faster than Andrea, just as we were told.
Harriet + Grace > Jennifer > Robyn > Andrea

questions.question: Short basketball players don't exist. There are short football players. Which statements are true?
choices: There are football players that aren't basketball players.
All basketball players are football players.
A short person can't be a football player.
questions.explanation:
The illustration shows that there are football players that aren't basketball players.

The answer is 'There are football players that aren't basketball players'.

questions.question: All birds with wings fly. There are black birds. Which statement is true?
choices: Anything that isn't black isn't a bird.
Anything without wings isn't a bird.
All birds with wings are black.
questions.explanation:
The illustration clearly shows that there are birds that are black and there are others types of birds as well. There are birds with wings, and black birds (not necessarily with wings). Not every bird with wings is necessarily black. Therefore none of the above statements are true.

The answer is 'None of the above'.
